newsitem.title: CONGO: Congo ex-leader Sassou still sees obstacle to talks.
newsitem.headline: Congo ex-leader Sassou still sees obstacle to talks.

text.p: Former Congolese president Denis Sassou Nguesso said on Monday that he did not see how negotiations could go ahead while President Pascal Lissouba accused him of trying to stage a coup.

"I don't see how one can negotiate on this basis, being accused of staging a coup d'etat," Sassou Nguesso told Reuters by telephone from his home in Brazzaville. "I am open to all negotiations, but I reject negotiations on an erroneous basis."
Sassou Nguesso's militias have fought government troops in the capital for the past five days, killing one French peacekeeping soldier and an unknown number of Congolese fighters and civilians.

Sassou Nguesso, who says his men are fighting in self defence, said he had respected an overnight truce at the request of Bernard Kolelas, Brazzaville's mayor and head of a committee trying to mediate between the two sides.

"We saw that Lissouba's militias were not respecting the ceasefire, so we responded," Sassou Nguesso said, adding that his forces had maintained their positions. He said these included the northern suburbs and part of the city centre.
He denied that his forces had artillery, although shells have hit the city centre and one exploded across the Zaire river in Kinshasa, capital of the neighbouring Democratic Republic of the Congo.
He said that he would do everything in his power to help French forces trying to evacuate foreigners. "I am greatly concerned for civilians, whether they are Congolese or foreigners," he said.
"I am in direct contact with the French ambassador and he even asked me to put some French families under my protection."
The fighting was triggered on Thursday when soldiers surrounded Sassou Nguesso's house in the search for his militiamen in the runup to July elections.
"They said they surrounded my house to arrest certain people, but now Lissouba says it was a coup d'etat, how can he change like that. How could I stage a coup from my bed?" he asked.
